sources.title: Zocdoc
sources.span: US platform where patients find and book in-person or telemedicine medical or dental appointments; doctors paid subscription fees 2007-2019, then the company moved to a per-new-patient referral fee; search covers doctors in over 100 specialties; telehealth video launched May 2020.

sources.title: Zocdoc Pay-Per-Booking for Providers: Fees & Cancellations
sources.span: Providers pay when a new patient books with a new provider; no upfront or subscription cost; the amount varies by specialty and location; the fee is charged at the moment of booking because it is described as a marketing fee, not based on visit outcome; practices can set monthly spend caps, pause spend, or disable individual providers.
sources.span_locator: Sections: how the fee works; cancellations; spend controls

sources.title: Does Zocdoc Verify Insurance? How Plan Matching Works
sources.span: Matching uses the plan the patient selects at search plus the plans providers list as accepted; verification does not guarantee in-network coverage; an appointment may appear in-network at booking and the office may later determine it is not; final in-network status is confirmed by the insurer and the provider office.
sources.span_locator: Sections: how matching works; what it does not guarantee

sources.title: Zocdoc Now Powers Real-Time Appointment Booking for Patients on Yelp
sources.span: Yelp users can book appointments from provider pages and from Yelp Assistant, an AI-powered chatbot, with real-time availability; company states appointments are typically scheduled within 24-72 hours; CEO quote: healthcare too often breaks at the start, when patients are ready to act but cannot easily transact.

sources.title: Zocdoc Launches The AI-Informed Patient Report
sources.span: Company-commissioned Censuswide survey of 1,186 US adults and 1,000 US providers in February 2026 reports 26% of patients have used AI to ask health-related questions and 23% have hidden that use from their doctor.

sources.title: Zocdoc unveils first-ever payer deal for appointment booking
sources.span: Blue Shield of California embedded booking into its member portal so members can schedule with in-network providers, with a 90-day booking window and more than one million hours of bookable time; members otherwise rely on health plan provider directories to find in-network care.

sources.title: Zocdoc BBB Complaints
sources.span: 153 complaints in three years. Provider complainants write of being 'charged me 3 times for clients I couldn't see' (2026-07-02), a 'fee jump of over 200%' (2026-05-14), and 'I still get charged' for out-of-network patients. Patient complainants report being seen by a 'completely different person than I expected' and slots that vanish and reappear 'all within a minute' (2026-04-30).

sources.title: ZocDoc Patients Reviews and Complaints
sources.span: 34 complaints, 1.6/5, 2% resolved. Recurring themes summarized as 'Listed as in-network but charged out-of-network fees', 'Mismatched specialty led to unexpected $75 copay', charges 'regardless of appointment outcome', and 'Appointment cancelled minutes before with no explanation'.

sources.title: Is Zocdoc Worth It? Pricing, Features & Best Alternative in 2026
sources.span: States a pay-per-booking model with per-new-patient fees 'range between $35 and $110' depending on specialty and region, criticizes that 'fees are not listed until late in the sign-up process' and that there is 'no standardized pricing structure', and frames smaller practices as preferring predictable costs. Publisher sells a competing scheduling product and promotes it as the alternative.

sources.title: My Experience Using ZocDoc To Help Grow My Practice
sources.span: First-person practice-owner account: signed up after a sales call because acquisition was measurable; tracked a no-show rate roughly three times higher than paid-search patients; 'only 6% became repeat patients over a year'; discontinued after the pricing model changed because the per-booking economics would 'lose money' once no-shows and overhead were counted.
sources.span_locator: Sections: why I signed up; the numbers; why I left

sources.title: Zocdoc Alternatives: Find & Book a Doctor Online
sources.span: FAQ headings written in patient question form: 'How do I find doctors that take my insurance?', 'Can I book a doctor online the same day?', 'Which is better, Zocdoc or Healthgrades?', 'Do I need an account to book an appointment online?'. Category map: booking-first tools versus research-first directories versus same-day urgent care versus cash-pay.

sources.title: 'Ghost networks' make finding mental health care harder
sources.span: Named patients spent '10 to 20 hours calling 60 clinicians' and went 16 months without treatment; a parent gave up and used an out-of-network provider for his child; directory testing found 40 of 50 listed providers unreachable or unable to provide the service, and 39 of 50 children's providers unreachable or unwilling to schedule; state enforcement of directory-accuracy law is described as weak.
sources.span_locator: Case studies; testing statistics; enforcement paragraphs

sources.title: Second Circuit Shuts Down Whistleblower's Attack on Zocdoc's Booking Fees
sources.span: A physician whistleblower alleged a 'secret caste system' steering federal-program patients toward providers paying higher per-booking fees; HHS-OIG advisory opinions in 2019 and 2023 found the model implicated but did not violate the Anti-Kickback Statute because fees were set in advance, at fair market value, and not based on volume or value of referrals; the Second Circuit affirmed dismissal.

sources.title: Zocdoc Software Pricing, Alternatives & More 2026
sources.span: Listing carries zero user reviews and no sentiment data; the page states that with no reviewer feedback available the support experience cannot be characterized. Alternatives surfaced by the directory are practice-management products (Jane App, ModMed, AestheticsPro), not patient-side booking marketplaces.

sources.title: Doctors Accepting New Patients Near Me - Book Appointments Online
sources.span: A target-owned landing page built around the literal query string 'doctors accepting new patients near me' and ranking for it in general web search. Evidence used here is the query pattern itself, not any claim made on the page. Page body was not retrievable (HTTP 403); only the indexed title and URL were observed.
sources.span_locator: Indexed page title and URL slug

sources.title: Find Spanish speaking doctors : By Language
sources.span: Indexed landing page title indicates a language filter for Spanish-speaking providers. Page body was not retrievable (HTTP 403); no Spanish-language buyer behavior, query, or review evidence was found.

sources.span: Unsupported model expansion: uninsured patients may search for the cheapest route to a non-urgent visit. No behavioral, review, query, or independent source in this manifest evidences this job for the declared perimeter.
